name: פישוט ביטוי רציונלי – מכפלת שני שברים אלגבריים וצמצום (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Write the following expression in an equivalent form in which all common factors have been cancelled.

\({{CT:0}}\cdot {{CT:1}} =\) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Factorise every numerator and every denominator first, then cancel the factors common to the numerator and the denominator.
Step 1 — Factorise each part
  • Perfect square \((a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2\):

    \[ {{CT:2}}={{CT:3}} \]

  • Difference of squares twice, \(a^4-b^4=\left(a^2\right)^2-\left(b^2\right)^2=(a^2-b^2)(a^2+b^2)\) and \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\):

    \[ {{CT:4}}={{CT:5}} \]

  • Common factor \(a\):

    \[ {{CT:6}}={{CT:7}} \]

  • \(a-b\) cannot be factorised further.
Step 2 — Write the expression in factored form
The first step is to write all expressions in factored form

\[ \frac{{CT:3}}{{CT:5}}\cdot\frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:8}}=\frac{(a-b)^2\cdot a\,(a+b)}{(a-b)(a+b)(a^2+b^2)\cdot(a-b)} \]

Step 3 — Cancel the common factors
Next we look for common factors in the numerator and denominator: \((a-b)^2\) in the numerator cancels with \((a-b)\cdot(a-b)\) in the denominator, and \((a+b)\) cancels as well (for the values of \(a,b\) where these factors are not zero). This gives

\[ {{CT:9}} \]

No factor of \(a\) divides \(a^2+b^2\), so nothing else cancels.

(Note, this question is very famous, and has appeared in the majority of algebra texts since Van Schooten introduced it in his textbook in Principia Matheseos Universalis (1651).  See Heller, H.F. (1940) Concerning the Evolution of the Topic of Factoring in Textbooks of Elementary Algebra Publish in England and the United States from 1631 to 1890. PhD, Columbia University.)

on_true.feedback: Your answer is equivalent to the correct answer, but it is not written in simplified form.  Perhaps you should try to factor the expressions further.
